# Proposed architecture decision

**Status: Proposed — project acceptance required.**

Engine 0.9.0; catalog 0.6.0; services 0.9.0; analysis 0.2.0.
Input SHA-256: 00e0e33f3acc4dbd27dc7c1de3d38092ad4f180821bd647a22d91dff17d5193e.

## Original result

PROVISIONAL STACK — unresolved critical constraints require review before production\. modular\_monolith recommendation selected from 204 complete compatible plans; month\-12 infrastructure planning band USD 55\.25–62\.02/month\.
Result: ok_with_warnings.

- frontend: React Native — Covers requested targets android with native rendering\. Team languages: javascript, python\. Selected after supporting\-service compatibility and whole\-plan infrastructure cost scoring\. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data\-flow/control exceptions\.
- backend: Django — Provides a python application runtime for the other profile\. Language familiarity and delivery complexity were compared across compatible whole plans\. Selected after supporting\-service compatibility and whole\-plan infrastructure cost scoring\. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data\-flow/control exceptions\.
- database: Supabase Pro PostgreSQL — relational persistence via Supabase Pro, one regional PostgreSQL project\.  Database drivers and host deployment were checked as a combination\. Selected after supporting\-service compatibility and whole\-plan infrastructure cost scoring\. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data\-flow/control exceptions\.
- hosting: DigitalOcean App Platform regional containers — Matches managed\_cloud with provider digitalocean; reviewed primary compute region blr\. Required runtimes and separate database deployment were checked\. Selected after supporting\-service compatibility and whole\-plan infrastructure cost scoring\. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data\-flow/control exceptions\.

Monthly infrastructure/operations band (activity fees additional): USD 55.25–62.02.

## Complete alternatives

- modular\_monolith\|react\-native\|django\|supabase\-pg\|do\-app\|blr; score 87; USD 55.25–62.02; selected.
- modular\_monolith\|react\-native\|express\|supabase\-pg\|do\-app\|blr; score 87; USD 55.25–62.02; alternative.
- modular\_monolith\|react\-native\|fastapi\|supabase\-pg\|do\-app\|blr; score 87; USD 55.25–62.02; alternative.

## Preference stability

Original winner retained in 25/25 tested settings; 1 observed winners. Counts are not confidence probabilities.

## Cost assumptions

- Horizon: expected month\-12 footprint; 730 hours/month\. No tax, development/on\-call labor, domain registration or new on\-prem hardware procurement is included\.
- Peak concurrency supplied: 200; not equated directly with requests/second\.
- RPS absent: authored daily\-active fraction 0\.2 of registered month\-12 users, floored at supplied peak concurrency \(400 active/day\); 50 requests/active user/day gives 0\.231 average RPS\. Neither fraction nor request rate is measured; explicit RPS overrides both\. Peak capacity is separate\.
- Data volume 100 GB supplied; egress 20 GB/month assumed at 0\.01 GB per year\-12 user, minimum 1 GB; backup retention 1 months assumed\.
- App Platform reference profile: 1 application/SSR and 1 background one\-GiB shared\-CPU containers, USD10/application container and USD10/background container monthly\. Fixed USD10 SKU is never scaled horizontally; if multiple instances are required use the USD12 SKU\. A 99/99\.9 target proposes single managed component instances relying on provider recovery, not application HA; higher targets add at least two instances\. The component SLA does not establish complete\-app availability, database failover or measured capacity\. Shared CPU, memory, connection limits and failover require load/restore tests before production\.
- App Platform builds/tests run in the native build stage within published build limits; no separately paid hosted CI or private container registry is enabled\. Regional app, Supabase and Spaces are separate configured boundaries\. Redacted logs are exported in batches with retries to the region\-pinned S3\-compatible Spaces bucket; ephemeral disk is only a bounded temporary buffer, never the durable archive\. Authored 1–4 KiB/request log payload and one monthly full restore are scenarios, not measured retention/volume\. Archive is a single USD5 Spaces subscription; DB seven\-day backups remain the Supabase tier policy\.
- Supabase Pro is one specific regional project, not a self\-hosted PostgreSQL alias\. Micro/Medium connection pools and CPU/RAM require validation; limit application pools and prefer transaction pooling\. Default DB backups are daily/seven days \(provider assumption overriding generic one\-month backup assumption for DB only\); no explicit month\-retention extension is accepted by this profile\. Object backup is separately charged\. No HIPAA Pro eligibility or contractual SLA is claimed\.
- OTP volume unknown, assumed range 0 to twice the year\-12 users: upper 4000 messages/month\. SMS rate is an explicit unquoted planning envelope; DLT, taxes and country routing may add fees\.
- Headline estimate and budget fit cover infrastructure/operations only\. Payment and SMS activity fees are separately itemized scenarios and excluded from this total; missing volumes are assumptions, not measured expenditure\.
- 100 GB file storage included once, then USD \.0213/GB\.
- 250 GB uncached allowance once; no additional cached allowance assumed\. Includes database\-to\-application plus direct client traffic within authored envelope; actual routing must be measured\.
- 8 GB included once; application data distribution between DB/files unknown, database uses 50–100% total data\.
- All month\-12 users conservatively treated as monthly active auth users; 100k included once\.
- Always\-on one\-GiB fixed worker containers; packed transactional outbox and telemetry reference footprint charged once\. Memory/startup/batch headroom and restart recovery require validation\.
- App Platform team transfer allowances pooled once, decimal GB converted to GiB\. Conservatively charges full app traffic plus archive uploads here; source Supabase backup download is separately charged there\. No Spaces/Droplet allowance is mixed into app transfer\.
- Assumed USD/SMS planning envelope only; verify country, tax, DLT and provider quote\. No currency conversion or MSG91 tariff is claimed\.
- One Spaces subscription bundles regional redacted logs and file backup storage; 250 GiB storage and 1024 GiB outbound included once\. Not an extra Supabase database backup or unlimited log index\.
- One USD 25 Pro organization/project; charge 730 hours of Micro \(\.01344/h\), or Medium \(\.0822/h\) when peak >=1000, minus one USD 10 compute credit\. Tier threshold is an unvalidated capacity hypothesis\.
- One full archive restore/download per month at upper bound; 1024\-GiB Spaces outbound allowance once\. Additional restore cycles need an explicit quote\.
- One\-GiB shared\-CPU application/SSR containers\. USD10 fixed SKU, one instance per component, no horizontal scaling\. Reference 50 RPS/1000 peak users is unvalidated; database/realtime are external\.
- Stored archive bytes above the single 250\-GiB allowance; includes authored 1–4 KiB redacted log events per API request plus retained file snapshots\.

## Blockers, validation and owner actions

- critical: The proposed regional log/file archive requires an implemented, pinned and tested S3\-compatible exporter/SDK, IAM, retry/backpressure, deletion retention and restore workflow\. The reviewed OpenTelemetry S3 exporter is alpha; no durable local worker disk, indexed log search, archive delivery or successful restore is assumed verified\. Shared one\-GiB container capacity and end\-to\-end availability remain unmeasured\.
- critical: MSG91 OTP is proposed provisionally: end\-to\-end india data residency is NOT established\. Verify tenant/merchant eligibility, processing, logs, backups, delivery partners and contracts before production\. This warning is an explicit exception to verified residency, not approval\.
- critical: Supabase Auth \+ application JWT verification is proposed provisionally: end\-to\-end india data residency is NOT established\. Verify tenant/merchant eligibility, processing, logs, backups, delivery partners and contracts before production\. This warning is an explicit exception to verified residency, not approval\.
- critical: Supabase regional Storage \+ signed direct uploads is proposed provisionally: end\-to\-end india data residency is NOT established\. Verify tenant/merchant eligibility, processing, logs, backups, delivery partners and contracts before production\. This warning is an explicit exception to verified residency, not approval\.
- critical: Only regional application/project placement is reviewed\. Supabase/Neon and hosting CDN, control plane, logs, support, backups and network processing do not have verified end\-to\-end residency; resolve this explicit provisional boundary before production\.
- critical: This paid managed tier is a planning proposal, not validated capacity or an availability SLA\. Validate pool limits, concurrent clients, CPU/memory, backup restore and the requested p95/availability before deployment; no automatic HA replicas are assumed\.
- warning: The output proposes technical control designs only\. It does not certify compliance, establish legal applicability, execute contracts, or replace an audit\. Implement controls and obtain scope\-specific review\.
- warning: Low\-memory device suitability requires an actual device benchmark; no framework is credited with unmeasured RAM/latency performance\.
- warning: Planning bands combine published reference rates and explicitly authored allowances; they are not regional provider quotes or measured workload capacity\. Validate sizing, merchant/SMS eligibility, storage, requests and current tariffs before purchase\.
- info: Availability and build/usage limits must still be checked for the configured deployment; no SLA is inferred from the product name\.
- requirements\.availability, requirements\.file\_media\_storage: Implement the regional archive boundary and run the synthetic failure/restore drill\. The estimate is not proof that the archive exists or survives failures\.
- infrastructure\.data\_residency, requirements\.auth: Request the scoped vendor data\-flow and configuration evidence\. Review a regional alternative without changing the original residency requirement\.
- infrastructure\.data\_residency, requirements\.auth: Request the scoped vendor data\-flow and configuration evidence\. Review a regional alternative without changing the original residency requirement\.
- infrastructure\.data\_residency, requirements\.file\_media\_storage: Request the scoped vendor data\-flow and configuration evidence\. Review a regional alternative without changing the original residency requirement\.
- infrastructure\.data\_residency: Review the scoped catalog evidence, workload and configuration; resolve the condition and rerun the unchanged input\.
- scale\.peak\_concurrent\_users, requirements\.availability: Review the scoped catalog evidence, workload and configuration; resolve the condition and rerun the unchanged input\.

## Limits and acceptance

- Exploratory analysis only. The original recommendation and original requirements are unchanged.
- Priority stability counts a finite one-at-a-time sweep; it is not a probability, confidence score or exhaustive sensitivity analysis.
- The tradeoff front covers all complete candidates in this finite reviewed catalog, minimizing cost upper bound and operated components while maximizing the ORIGINAL-priority heuristic score. It does not establish real-world optimality or measured architecture quality.
- Functional experiments try eligible single/pair edits only: phone login to email/password, payments off, offline support off, full-text search off, or unsupported ML off. They are changed projects, never solutions satisfying the original brief.
- Within Decision Lab functional experiments, compliance, infrastructure/residency/provider, tenant isolation, availability, budget, team and timeline are never relaxed. A usable hypothetical result is not legal, security or production approval.
- No user assertion authenticates vendor/tenant evidence. Missing contracts, capacity calibration and independent review remain unresolved.
- engine_evaluations counts top-level scenario trials; the baseline recommendation may additionally evaluate one separately labeled budget proposal. Budget proposals are outside the functional-experiment sweep and never change the baseline brief.
- The generated ADR is Proposed; no stakeholder acceptance, implementation or deployment is inferred.

Acceptance, independent review, vendor eligibility, implementation and deployment remain owner tasks. No acceptance is recorded.

Language familiarity 5.00/5 and implementation-complexity rubric 2.75/5; short delivery/beginner-complexity and manual Markdown-conversion penalties are explicit heuristics; supported server-language depth 1 gives ecosystem reuse bonus 0.
Static delivery avoids application writes; embedded-writer and growth triggers are ordinal review heuristics, not published capacity limits.
No latency SLA or measured framework throughput is credited; embedded-write concurrency is a review heuristic. Low-memory clients require measurement, not an assumed framework benchmark.
Operational burden 1/5+; no existing-system reuse bonus. Server ecosystem reuse bonus 0; fewer self-operated systems are favored without DevOps. Additional service operating penalty 0.
Baseline configured controls: 3; explicit reviewed tenant isolation: 4. No certification/audit credit is assigned.

Shared one-GiB container capacity and end-to-end availability remain unmeasured.

limitations: Exploratory analysis only. The original recommendation and original requirements are unchanged.
Priority stability counts a finite one-at-a-time sweep; it is not a probability, confidence score or exhaustive sensitivity analysis.

The tradeoff front covers all complete candidates in this finite reviewed catalog, minimizing cost upper bound and operated components while maximizing the ORIGINAL-priority heuristic score. It does not establish real-world optimality or measured architecture quality.

Functional experiments try eligible single/pair edits only: phone login to email/password, payments off, offline support off, full-text search off, or unsupported ML off. They are changed projects, never solutions satisfying the original brief.

Within Decision Lab functional experiments, compliance, infrastructure/residency/provider, tenant isolation, availability, budget, team and timeline are never relaxed. A usable hypothetical result is not legal, security or production approval.
